title: Compact command column, complete planet editor and diplomacy repairs
synopsis: Info, reserves and signals share a narrower right column. Staff can choose every known world. Galaxy allocation starts at 1:2; diplomacy and capture XP follow the documented war rules.
changes: SF-117/SF-118/SF-123: Per-resource asteroid counters remain in their rings. The page keeps more space below the header. Info, resources and Recent Signals now share a 248px column, widening the centre; the Info card returns to the header on small screens.

SF-119: Isolated Havoc confirmation, per-race ships, resources, roids, research, construction, speed and central apply/restore checks passed. Fixed the owner research/building mirror and the research progress object; preserved stable legacy alliance identities across repeated staff saves.

SF-120: Alliance proposals require acceptance. Relations show war bonuses and remaining ticks. War requires a shuffled universe and five planets per side, permits one primary target with optional target allies, and lasts 48 ticks. First/higher-ranked targets gain +5 capture points / +25% capture XP; secondary cases gain +3 / +15%; other targets during war receive -5 / -25%. Undefended captures earn XP, ship destruction alone does not, and asteroid distribution cannot make a resource field negative.

SF-121: New shuffled galaxies begin at cluster 1, galaxy 2. Legacy shuffled galaxy keys are repaired atomically with planet slots, treasury and stronghold references preserved. Galaxy 1:1 stays pinned; this is not a reset or reshuffle.

SF-122: The planet editor loads all 1,453 current and retired catalogue worlds. Changing type updates the survey and bonuses while preserving other colony assets. Unknown worlds and duplicate unique worlds are rejected.

Validation: 565 automated tests passed; 25 game pages rendered without browser errors; five viewport widths had no document overflow. Concurrent sessions and the remaining SF-068 shared-workflow audit are not certified by this fixture.

title: Audit repairs for scans, galaxy controls and layout
synopsis: Galaxy sweeps charge eligible scans only, fleet reports show actual known movements, and galaxy controls persist and enforce their roles.
changes: SF068-M01–M05: Single scans and sweeps share eligibility checks. Sweeps skip ineligible target/type pairs before charging. Incoming scans target home once per sweep; Jumpgate uses travelling fleets rather than docked ships. Unknown composition/guards stay unknown. New reports use real line breaks; historical escaped breaks remain readable.

SF068-SOC03–SOC05: Practice exile voting charges Galaxy Fund, not Alliance Fund. GC galaxy name/message and Development Minister donation-resource policy are centrally persisted. The deposit endpoint enforces disabled resources. Shared exile approvals and central delayed alliance donations remain open audit work.
SF068-SOC06: Staff structure placement follows active claim slot policy, including slots 16–20 for galaxy 1:1, and retains existing assets.
SF068-L01/L02: Repositioned the decorative rail circle to avoid document overflow. Population survey content and compact tax controls can shrink and wrap at intermediate widths.

title: Alliance income controls and cleaner galaxy navigation
synopsis: Separate stronghold bribes from ordinary alliance tax, configure access to each tab, browse occupied galaxies and allocate refinery bonus CU without obsolete research gates.
changes: SF-116: Real population tick observations are retained until central settlement. Several ticks between colony reports now convert their recorded full-housing surplus once, instead of treating those observed ticks as missing history. No unrecorded past growth is fabricated.
SF-068 (partial audit repair): Rendering construction no longer treats building projects as ship orders or erases their remaining work. The broader manual audit remains in progress.

SF-115: Bonus CU uses the same building eligibility as ordinary construction. Refineries and other facilities no longer require obsolete research gates. Active and queued projects retain their reserved slots.

SF-112: Alliance tax shows projected revenue before saving. Strong Encouragement charges own members in the active stronghold galaxy at 0–7.5% in half-percent steps, with a separate configurable rank permission. Ordinary tax and bribes settle once with each recorded colony tick.

SF-112: The alliance income ledger separates ordinary tax, bribes and total. Structure prices use only projected ordinary tax, never bribes. Projections identify how many members have reported income; historical missing ticks are not invented.

SF-113: Each alliance tab has its own configurable rank permission. Inaccessible tabs are hidden and a revoked active tab falls back to an allowed tab. Existing server action permissions remain enforced.

SF-114: Galaxy Browser and Alliance Intel show occupied planets, structures and memorials only. Navigation uses existing galaxies and stops at the ends; coordinate display uses 1:1:1 while internal directory keys remain stable.
SF-110: System messages stay in the journal but are excluded from Recent Signals.
SF-111: Round reset clears every ingame forum scope. The previously requested one-time forum cleanup has already completed; this release performs no further reset.

title: Keep galaxy 1:1 outside redistribution
synopsis: Manual and automatic shuffle preserve all planets already in galaxy 1:1. The user-requested round reset starts a fresh charter generation.
changes: SF-109: Galaxy 1:1 is excluded before randomisation and temporary coordinate staging. Its planets keep their exact coordinates and data during both manual shuffle and automatic tick-12 distribution.
The explicitly requested round reset clears current colonies and shared round state and prepares new charters. Accounts, ownership keys, memorials and historical generation-scoped receipts remain.

title: Ecological base growth at full housing
synopsis: A targeted population correction creates positive base growth without Biodomes and supplies the Galaxy Fund at full housing. The moving navigation bar is substantially shallower.
changes: SF-107: Ecological base growth uses habitability, biodiversity, moisture, inverse rockiness and founding population. Biodomes add growth; research and the existing planet growth modifier multiply the result. Even a zero-Biodome planet has positive potential growth. At full housing this growth converts to Galaxy Fund resources, including ordinary levy zero, with fractions carried forward and no extra residents removed. Frontend, settlement, projections and manual use the same base calculation.
SF-108: Desktop development tiles are 56 pixels high. The full-size Info panel overlays the right rail instead of making all five tiles tall. The moving banner remains transparent.

title: Alliance Shipyards and cooperation milestones
synopsis: Shared production uses the existing Alliance Fleet; Universe alliance statistics, transparent navigation and rewarded quest chains improve command.
changes: SF-100: Owner, HC and Officer can fund mixed member-race ship orders through Alliance Shipyards using combined member factories. A race-column matrix allocates hulls to a member’s existing fourth fleet and Launch Bay. Alliance Ships cannot transfer to Base or personal fleets. Sales return 50% catalog resources to Alliance Fund after 12 ticks; delivery, loss and sale counters reconcile once with launch and readiness fences.

SF-101: Universe offers Total overview, Planets and Alliances submenus. The total view stacks the original statistics with the top ten alliances and selected alliance member details: ruler, planet, asteroids, score, population and XP. Missing reports remain unknown.

SF-102 and SF-098 correction: The complete header follows the viewport without clipping or internal scrolling. Its wrapper background is transparent, while navigation cards and Info retain readable surfaces.

SF-103: Education adds saved workforce assignment goals at 60%, 70%, 80%, 90% and 100%. Capacity research alone does not complete these goals. Every step has escalating resources, CU and RP rewards in the existing reward treasury.
SF-104: Alliance cooperation replaces the repeated forum dispatch ladder with one rewarded alliance-forum post objective. Existing claim history is retained.

SF-105: Alliance cooperation counts real Defence departures to current alliance members, starting at zero. The first fleet matches the existing defence quest reward; 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 fleets grant increasing resources, CU and RP. Fake Defence, rejected launches and cancelled scheduled departures do not count.

title: Population levies and quiet order confirmations
synopsis: Population conversion, fleet navigation and admin controls improve alongside an audited treasury and shared order receipts.
changes: SF-093: Ministers choose 0–5 residents per planet per 24 ticks, with a rolling five-resident cap. Verified unused growth at full housing converts into Galaxy Fund resources even at a zero ordinary levy. The population register separates actual levies, overflow conversions and next-tick projections; unobserved historical ticks are not invented.

SF-094: A read-only audit matched all nine round-24 trade receipts with Universal Bank collected fees: 3,850 metal, 2,620 crystal and 2,500 eonium. The older zero-fee direct-bank receipt predates the 5% default deployment.
SF-096: Authorised planet editors can apply a settled government immediately, clearing pending anarchy. Reset and command identifiers prevent stale replays from changing later player revolutions.
SF-097: The first Galaxy Browser opening follows the authenticated home galaxy rather than the practice seed; subsequent manual browsing is retained.
SF-098: Development navigation and Info stay together at the top while scrolling, with a bounded scrollable header on smaller screens.

SF-099: Accepted construction, research, asteroid, ship, fleet and trade orders share a persisted background confirmation ledger. They no longer open order popups or add order news; errors and ordinary completion or combat reports remain visible.

title: Fresh game data without reloading command
synopsis: Page navigation refreshes game data while keeping the site and theme in place. Loading recovery, compact reports and treasury settlement improve command operations.
changes: SF-092: Each game-page opening reads fresh central data. Concurrent navigation shares a read; stale account, reset and navigation responses are rejected. Local tick, resources and pending projects remain intact. Site and theme caches retain their previous settings, superseding SF-091.

SF-083: Adjacent game stylesheets are bundled without changing their cascade order, the runtime download starts earlier, and hidden-page planet artwork loads lazily. Initial directory reads recover one transient failure, stalled reads have a bounded timeout, and directory retry avoids reloading the document. The release now includes its database migration beside the hosting manifest.
SF-084: The current-structures register uses content-sized rows, smaller icons and compact costs while retaining all effect text.
SF-085: Construction order reports use readable full-width news cards in a bounded scrollable modal.
SF-086: Spaceport has a third Alliance Fund tab for personal resource exchange with finite alliance reserves.

SF-087: The alliance-page exchange is reserved for Owner, HC and Officer exchanges between alliance reserves and the Universal Bank. Atomic settlement, rank, reserve and revision checks protect shared balances.
SF-089: Fees from personal fund exchanges are deposited in the Universal Bank in the received resource, atomically with the exchange.
SF-090: Galaxy Fund exchange charges 1%, rounded up to whole resource units. Alliance personal exchange retains 2.5%; direct bank exchanges follow the configured standard 5%.

SF-088: Quartus Relay joins the original worlds with its own survey and artwork, the same 20% battle-salvage eligibility as Earth, and no separate interface theme. Existing planets are not reassigned.

title: Compact treasuries, population history and action reports
synopsis: Ten completed requests improve resource trading, settings and visual clarity while keeping order reports on screen.
changes: SF-067: Navigation artwork preserves its proportions across the game themes.
SF-071: Compact responsive navigation keeps Info beside Planet Settings when space allows.
SF-074: Galaxy Fund and Spacing Bank use matching resource rows.
SF-075: Spaceport separates fund actions from the bank and restores 1:1 personal-resource trades with finite Galaxy Fund reserves and atomic duplicate-safe receipts.
SF-077: The standard Spacing Bank fee is 5%. Legacy default zero settings upgrade once without changing reserves; explicit later staff settings remain respected.
SF-078: Alliance Fund donations and exchanges use compact matching rows; exchanges deduct a rounded-up 2.5% fee while retaining permission and reserve checks.
SF-079: Orders display their newly generated news report without reloading. A bounded wait retains the refresh fallback when no report appears.
SF-080: Planetary Survey charts recorded population from tick zero through the present. New planets and resets retain the founding measurement; unrecorded past ticks remain visible gaps.
SF-081: Planet Reset has a readable inline confirmation checkbox.
SF-082: Planet Settings uses compact responsive cards and consistent controls.

title: Bugfix · Reliable bank data responses
synopsis: The bank handles interrupted or HTML responses safely and keeps exchange submissions separate from data retries.
changes: Bank reads validate response type and session status before parsing data. A transient read failure receives one bounded retry; sign-in errors offer a sign-in link.
Bank endpoint failures return controlled JSON errors, and normal bank reads no longer issue schema-creation statements or redundant reserve initialization writes.
Exchange submissions are never automatically repeated by read recovery. Existing revision checks, transaction receipts and duplicate protection remain in place.

title: Bugfix · Recover interrupted command assets
synopsis: Transient stylesheet, artwork and workspace-bootstrap failures now receive bounded recovery attempts.
changes: Same-origin stylesheets and public artwork retry up to twice after a network load failure. Successful recovery is recorded in the error log.
The game runtime waits for the workspace bootstrap. If that script cannot load after three attempts, startup stops visibly rather than using the wrong browser save.
Existing runtime retries remain bounded; unrelated scripts, external resources and private image endpoints are not generically retried.

title: Bugfix · Staff connection recovery
synopsis: Staff workspaces render independently of player screens and recover when a slow connection completes after the startup timeout.
changes: Staff controlcenters render their own content without running every player-page renderer or reloading for a player-theme change.
Hidden staff frames do not wait for animation frames to become usable. A late successful connection can recover a timeout; actual failed scripts remain blocked.
The connection panel and error log identify which startup stage failed instead of showing only a generic theme message.

title: Bugfix · Shared staff controlcenter startup
synopsis: Admin and Alliance Controlcenters now use one workspace initializer, independent of the original ingame Administration preference.
changes: Both staff controlcenters use the same initializer and explicitly retain embedded workspace mode when the original ingame Administration menu is enabled or disabled.
An empty round no longer leaves staff waiting indefinitely for a player theme. Player onboarding and staff access checks remain enforced.

title: Command foundation · Part 1 of 2
synopsis: Seven completed tasks covering development queues, galaxy ownership, personal resets and alliance fleet organisation.
changes: Shared spacing rules across game pages and themes.
Four total construction and research slots, including the active project, with queued progression and cancellation.
The actual Info box now sits beside Planet Settings with its data and clocks.
Exclusive stronghold claims, retained inactive reservations, two-party empty transfers and audited conflict resolution.
Galaxy 1:1 uses player slots 1–10, ghost slots 11–15 and structure slots 16–20 only under its stronghold policy; existing occupied slots remain protected.
Personal reset is instant before the ticker starts, preserving alliance membership; afterwards it waits 72 hours and removes only the resetting player from the alliance.
Battlegroup membership, approvals, leadership and attack-booking linkage with current permission and revision guards.

title: Command interface and delivery · Part 2 of 2
synopsis: Seven completed tasks covering performance, themes, resource exchange, source ownership, battle planning and alliance news.
changes: Bounded public-data caching, content ETags and omission of unreferenced old portal runtime bundles while retaining live-page compatibility.
Game startup waits for the runtime and authoritative theme before showing the command interface.
Three separate Metal, Crystal and Eonium exchange panels with independent inputs, quotes and feedback.
The duplicate Planet sidebar section is removed while the five main navigation tiles remain.
Twelve canonical portal, game and shared frontend inputs have separate source folders and one composed build; game seed generation is separated from portal pages.
Compact defender/attacker battle planning with four fleets per side, display filters, scan-count import and saved browser drafts; existing Starfall combat rules remain.
Tax and central stronghold changes deliver atomic alliance news and mail to current members, including the actor.

title: Bugfix · Spacing Bank stays visible
synopsis: The Spacing Bank Collective remains available when the Galaxy Fund refreshes instead of briefly appearing and disappearing.
changes: Ordinary game updates preserve the bank module and its entered exchange values.
Bank loading is guarded against stale account or page responses, and load failures remain visible with retry.
The fix preserves transaction permissions and revision checks. No round reset.

title: Bugfix · Correct production and development timing
synopsis: Ship production uses the documented factory formula instead of raw resource totals; construction and research use racial base rates and additive bonuses.
changes: Matching Light, Medium and Heavy factory pools include preparation work and pause when no relevant factories are assigned. Cruisers use Heavy factories.
Construction and research rates use documented race bases, additive workforce/government bonuses and a capped laboratory percentage. Starfall population and round modifiers remain.

Existing paid orders retain quantities, destinations, costs and completion percentage through a one-time migration. Historical mixed-order cost splits are approximated from their preserved total. No round reset.

title: Bugfix · Galaxy elections and ministers stay local
synopsis: Galactic Commander candidates and minister choices now show only planets in your own galaxy, including your own planet.
changes: Election candidates, ballots and minister choices are constrained to the current home galaxy.
Moving or exiling a planet clears its old votes and minister offices; stale server appointments are cleaned through the existing revision guard.
Galaxy identity and local politics no longer follow you into another galaxy. No round reset is performed.

title: Bugfix · Clear account registration feedback
synopsis: Registration now shows progress, a visible success confirmation and the next step, while preventing duplicate submissions.
changes: Register remains disabled until the form handler is ready; the form uses POST instead of the default GET.
REGISTERING… and an account-creation message remain visible during the request.
Success clears password fields and offers Continue to planet registration. Errors and required-field validation remain visible.

title: Bugfix · Unfolded navigation stays accessible
synopsis: The expanded game menu scrolls independently and no longer disappears behind the sidebar footer.
changes: The navigation uses its own scroll area while the footer keeps its own space.
Portal, Support, Manual and Sign out no longer overlap expanded menu entries.
The fix applies across game themes, including smaller viewports. No round reset is performed.

title: Bugfix · Registered planets and alliance creation
synopsis: Removes generated fake galaxy planets, restores the alliance creation form and repairs zero-price research levels. A requested round reset clears existing colony state.
changes: Empty galaxies stay empty; cached fixture rows remain hidden while connecting to the central directory.
The unaffiliated alliance creation form is visible and opens correctly.
Unfinished research levels use a positive RP cost, including Infrastructure level three.
One authorised round reset returns players to colony registration; accounts and reserved alliance Owner keys remain.

title: Command roster and split diagnostics
synopsis: Six completed improvements to staff presentation, saved diagnostics and compact game layouts.
changes: Contribution archive and original Unimatrix memorial artwork.
Responsive staff roster with role cards and responsibilities.
Separate AI tribute plaque and Omega Order medal.
Separate Portal and Game diagnostics with independent progress and labelled saved reports.
Compact colonial charter confirmation retaining its complete survey.
Government workforce and ministry panel spacing.

title: Bugfix · Reserve galaxy 1:1 for staff
synopsis: Ordinary new players no longer enrol in galaxy1:1. Existing staff planets remain where they are.
changes: New Player accounts begin outside galaxy1:1; staff accounts retain access to its registration slots.
The existing Multihunter planet at1:1:2 remains in place after checking its account role. No planet is moved or reset.
Existing planetary assets and alliance membership are preserved.

title: Alliance planning and staff control
synopsis: Five completed improvements: faster public pages, configurable staff permissions, clearer fleet panels, pa-tools attack planning and the in-game General forum.
changes: One-minute caches reduce repeated public asset decoding and public data requests. Private profiles, permissions and gameplay writes retain fresh authorisation.
Support and Multihunter permission nodes are configurable on Account ranks. Saves are audited and revision-checked; only Administrators can edit the matrix or grant Administrator rank.
Network Hub fleet panels and intel controls have consistent spacing across themes, with wrapped controls and scrollable tables.

The alliance attack tool now adapts pa-tools operations, scheduled openings, prereleases, consecutive wave bookings and shared ownership. Existing claims are imported; revisions prevent conflicting claims. The full Battlegroup page remains queued under SF-032.
General forum is available inside the game alongside the private galaxy and alliance forums. Private membership checks remain in place.

title: Bugfix · Research bonuses finish the active project
synopsis: Allocating enough bonus RP completes the slotted research level and frees its project slot.
changes: Bonus RP now clears the active research slot when that level completes, including levels below the branch maximum.
Surplus allocated RP remains attached to the next level; unspent bonus points remain in the bonus bank.
The current round is preserved.

title: Bugfix · Empty founding fleets and restored ministerial navigation
synopsis: New colonies begin without demonstration ships. The ministerial register opens correctly, followed by the requested round reset.
changes: Founding ships, the base fleet and all four fleets start empty. Ships must be built or granted through an explicit game action.
The Government ministerial-register button uses the game navigation handler.
The requested reset renews the round and registration drafts while preserving accounts and stored diagnostic reports.

title: Bugfix · Accurate diagnostics and progress feedback
synopsis: Fixes repeated historic errors, false layout warnings and incorrect report versions; shows real inspection progress.
changes: Current-page errors and historical errors are stored separately. Reloading no longer adds another timestamp to old errors.
Diagnostic samples report new errors from that page load. Closed disclosures, hidden controls and transparent elements no longer produce false viewport warnings.
Layout warnings identify the visible controls involved. Reports record the deployed version.
A progress bar advances after each completed browser page check and after the report is saved, with the current stage and completed count.
The current round is preserved.

title: Bugfix · Editable planet names
synopsis: Reference-world holders can edit their personal planet name during registration and in Planet Settings.
changes: The registration name field is editable for every world. A reference name is used as its initial suggestion.
The server keeps the entered player name instead of forcing the reference name. Planet Settings can rename an existing reference-world colony.
World type, artwork, unique reservation and special bonuses remain attached to the same world; naming cannot create a second copy.
The current round is preserved.

title: Staff diagnostics and ancestral world charters
synopsis: Adds a protected inspection console with stored reports, twenty Frontier environments, five Ultimate race capitals and recoverable scan sharing.
changes: Staff can run system diagnostics, inspect saved reports and export JSON. Checks cover internal links, anchors, missing assets, metadata and sampled browser runtime/layout observations.
All staff ranks may inspect reports without owning a planet; players cannot open the page or its API. Reports survive round resets.

Frontier Worlds now includes twenty active original environments. Five once-per-round Ancestral Thrones apply their racial theme and grant 10% ship resource discounts, multiplied with government discounts.
Catalogue families use generic names, and paged requests retrieve only the visible surveys. Assignment changes that alter a theme reload the game once.
Scan sharing retries a failed initial connection and offers a visible retry control. Confirmed server settings remain authoritative.
The user-requested reset removes active planets, renews registration and rerolls, releases world reservations and stops the ticker. Accounts, Owner recovery keys and diagnostic reports remain.
A general visual polish pass and expanded family artwork await explicit user authorisation after the reset.

title: Bugfix · Reliable game startup and restored modules
synopsis: Loads the ship catalogue and game modules together, restoring quests, workforce controls and unfolded navigation when individual scripts failed to load.
changes: The game loads one ordered runtime instead of seventeen separate scripts; failed downloads retry automatically without applying a partial startup.
Rendering starts after the complete runtime is initialised. The connection panel provides a retry button when downloads remain unavailable.
The browser receives a versioned runtime URL. Error logs identify failed files and JavaScript source locations.
The game loads a small world seed and receives the actual planet surveys with its directory, rather than parsing the complete reference catalogue on every visit.
Background polls pause when the page is hidden. This bugfix preserves the current round and does not perform another reset.

title: Bugfix · Faster loading and staff access corrections
synopsis: Fixes slow and temporarily unstyled portal pages, reduces unnecessary database work, and separates privileged documentation by staff role.
changes: Portal typography uses immediate theme-matched fallback fonts; external blocking font imports are removed. Large videos load only when played, with preload disabled.
Access auditing runs after the response through the Worker execution context. Schema and authenticated-request lookups are reused, and binary assets decode without per-byte array callbacks.
Players’ manual removes staff-only chapters, controls and editorial modules. Staff manual is served only after authentication and staff-role checks.
Administrator, Support and Multihunter manuals expose procedures relevant to that role, with a common permissions matrix and evidence-handling guide.
Spacing Bank policy and Site management remain Administrator responsibilities. Support has tickets and read-only staff audit; Multihunters has access, fleet investigation and read-only audit.
Staff tools continue to work without a personal planet. This documentation update does not reset the round again.

title: World charters, expanded quest offices and the Spacing Bank Collective
synopsis: Discover unique worlds, exclusive interfaces, detailed rewards, a finite universal resource exchange and a clearer staff portal.
changes: Final charter confirmation uses two columns: identity and controls on the left, planet artwork and full stats on the right.
The mobile confirmation stacks both panels and remains scrollable. Planet assignment and entered values stay unchanged.
Round-reset wording now reflects removal of planets followed by new charter registration.
Planet Overview displays the same assigned-world artwork as colonial registration, with type, habitability, growth modifier and starting housing.

Planet register: named Star Trek and Dune worlds, twenty once-per-round Borg/Undine worlds, Earth, Ultimate Arrakis and Unimatrix999 Homeworld. Lore-inspired ecology and generated gameplay survey values are labelled.

Registration stays fixed across refresh and permits three server-counted rerolls. Unique names and reservations prevent duplicate world charters. Ordinary worlds at 60% habitability or lower leave new selection; special worlds are exempt.

Arrakis has −1 tick fleet travel for the round; Earth receives 20% bonus salvage from destroyed attackers and defenders when it participates. Unique charter broadcasts conceal the holder and coordinates.
Exclusive Silver, Borg, Undine, Legendary, Ultimate and Unimatrix999 styles apply automatically and appear only for the corresponding holder and staff.

Every achievement office offers at least fifteen supported goals, in an ordered upper menu. The summary tab contains statistics. New rewards include resources, CU, RP, settlers and research-gated structures; blocked structures convert to their CU cost.

Spaceport adds the finite Spacing Bank Collective, starting at one million of each resource per round. Staff controls tax, values and limits; admins configure next-round starting reserves. Exchange receipts settle atomically.
Five-character read-only account IDs appear on profiles and command cards. Staff workspaces operate without a planet, and round settings display an inline saved timestamp.
Staff overview and the new portal Staff page show a full personnel roster and duties. Staff and the placeholder Round history page are linked in the top menu.
Galaxy Browser initially opens the player’s own galaxy and includes a Go to 1:1 button. Leading Of is omitted in the planetary command display.
Site management retains the news editor and adds global toggles for Round history demo examples and the simulated battle lab. Real completed round archives automatically replace fictional examples.

title: Planetary charters, population development and Astra Nexus
synopsis: A new round begins with 36 worlds, confirmed planetary registration, population taxes, galaxy redistribution and a redesigned alliance command.
changes: Every reset removes all planets, dummies and placeholders; accounts return to a confirmed identity, race, theme and assigned-world charter. Ticks begin stopped.
Thirty-six illustrated world types set 500–1,000 starting residents and environmental population-growth modifiers from −75% to +50%.
Biodomes generate settlers gradually; Population Development research adds five +20% levels. Research and population milestones reward CU/RP under Secretary of Development.

Minister of Development controls 0–5% population levy. Equal shares retain fractional debt; each collected resident funds 6 Metal, 4 Crystal and 2 Eonium. Politics and Government show statistics and graphs.
Spaceport hosts a separate Galaxy Fund module with centrally recorded deposits and eligible payouts.
Players begin in starting galaxies. Tick 12 redistributes players once, allocating galaxies and clusters; Admin Control provides confirmed manual shuffle.
Unaffiliated commands receive Join, Create and Recover modules. All known alliances are listed; recruitment requests appear as pending Recruits.
Alliance overview prioritises news and resource-income reports, with refinery, finance and population contributions.
Achievement categories have individual tabs. Shared page spacing, compact layouts and consistent theme fonts apply throughout the game.
Astra Nexus adds holographic command artwork, cyan-magenta lighting and a futuristic interface.

Ticker and planet status are merged into one command module, with Simulate Tick and Reset controls at the side. All news reports include lore, recorded outcomes and available event context. Internal links and anchors were audited and corrected.

title: Balanced ship tables and confirmed Havoc presets
synopsis: Clearer structure and ship statistics, percentage-based population damage and a race-aware ten-ship Havoc matrix.
changes: Current Structures has balanced columns, larger icons, resource-by-resource costs and compact structure artwork. Narrow screens use cards.
Public Shipstats and the staff Stats Editor have compact fixed-width columns and a Pop dmg% field.
Cruisers and Battleships deal 0.1% of defender starting population per surviving ship by default. Percentages sum up to 100%; other ship classes remain blank. Older overrides migrate once.
Havoc replaces class totals with ten ship quantities mapped to the corresponding named ships in each race.
Confirm setup validates all requested racial ships before applying. Invalid or missing matches block the complete application without partial changes.
Each confirmation saves the full Havoc form. The latest five browser-local setups are available in a dropdown; the sixth replaces the oldest. Loading requires a fresh confirmation before application.
Race colours distinguish Helion, Velari, Nexari, Kryth and Auralis in the editor and the Havoc matrix.

title: Government, Biodomes and diplomatic mail
synopsis: Population habitats, battle casualties, private player mail and clearer alliance operations.
changes: Government receives a colony register, housing cap, population income bonus and explicit workforce Confirm/Reset controls.
Biodomes house 50 residents, feature original artwork and lore, and add a balanced CU/RU quest line.
Cruisers and Battleships also target population. Structure killers damage Biodomes and their occupants; battle calculator and reports show both effects.
Diplomacy alerts both alliances, with target-player Mail, narrative reports and Planetarion-style capture/XP bonuses.
Private player Mail includes inbox, sent messages, replies and pagination. Admin force key reveal is audited without recording secrets.
Fleet roster is transposed; launch bay, fleet readiness and structure tables are compact. Universe adds largest planets and population growth/loss rankings.
Private intel affiliations and nicknames no longer inherit public membership data.
Worker bribery triggers a six-tick mining strike; Biodome sabotage destroys habitats and occupants, with dedicated successful-operation quests.
Population adds 1 CU and 1 RP per complete 100 residents; income shows separate refinery and Finance Centre contributions.

title: Order refresh, fleet roster and achievement receipts
synopsis: Clearer orders, resource income, building capacity and itemised achievement reward receipts.
changes: Successful asteroid, ship, construction, research and alliance structure orders save and reload the current game page. Draft edits and rejected orders do not reload.
Mining begins with Income per tick, styled like the Resource Bank and showing owned asteroid counts per resource.
Construction lists owned buildings, queued reservations, free slots, affordable quantities, next costs and bonus information.
All Ships moves the entire selected source fleet. Amount is ignored for that option; source and destination selections persist. Deployed fleets cannot transfer.
Fleet Roster lists ship names with separate Class, Target 1, Target 2 and Target 3 columns. Missing targets are blank.
Manual, bulk and automatic Achievement claims produce a festive receipt with claimed objectives, gold claim medals and exact totals by reward type.
New and reset rounds assign 0% workforce. Department limits are 25/50/35/60/50%; the available pool starts at 50% and reaches 100% through Population Management research.

title: Alliance fleet readiness and command interface
synopsis: Prioritised alliance fleets, clearer ticker status and refreshed diplomacy, treasury and navigation.
changes: Alliance Fleet is shown first. Player fleets 1–3 are collapsed behind a plus; fleets reported on a mission are hidden.
Fleet tables separate ship class and three target priorities; same-galaxy alliance defence shows ETA 5.
Ticker information displays state, current tick, interval, next tick, schedule and last processed tick, with visible action confirmations.
Galaxy Browser totals span the complete roster and optional intel columns.
Galaxy Politics uses a council briefing and clearer policy forms. Galaxy Fund shows reserve allocation and treasury cards.
Similar submenus share rounded theme-aware buttons and a clear selected state.

title: Alliance attack claims and fleet worksheet
synopsis: Private attack coordination, spreadsheet-style calculator inputs and stopped ticker after reset.
changes: Alliance Attack tool adds private targets and one active claim per player; administrators cannot bypass claim limits or claim permissions.
Owner, HC and Officer can manage operations by default; Members can claim targets. Recruitment ranks cannot claim by default.
Calculator uses one compact ship worksheet with Attacker and Defender columns, class colours, arrow-key navigation and spreadsheet paste.
Fresh game state explicitly stops the ticker and clears the scheduled start; resetting a round clears attack targets and claims.

title: Control panels, account ranks and player-only round
synopsis: Native portal staff headers, private alliance reservations, account roles and field-level planet audit.
changes: User control panel and Staff control panel have clear, non-duplicated submenus. The portal header aligns with the main content and account box.
Staff workspaces use native portal banners; game banners and ornate frames are removed. Fields, KPI boxes, keyholder controls and structure artwork are spaced consistently.
Alliance manager reserves up to five inactive alliances with encrypted personal keys, edits the current active alliance and adds up to two additional keyholders.
Account ranks include Player, Support, Multihunter and Administrator; only Administrators change ranks and at least one must remain.
Staff planet audit records committed field changes, previous/new values and the actor. Support and Multihunter can read the audit.
Requested cleanup removes non-player planets and alliances while preserving personal reservations. Practice planets no longer automatically return.
Reset leaves the ticker stopped with the previous schedule cleared. Manual or newly scheduled starts can enable it.
Battle calculator outputs simulated news reports only on its own page, without adding them to Journal. Uplink test reports remain in their test module.
Archive Forums lists only the current galaxy and alliance forums. The Foreign Affairs Galaxy Forum link is removed.

title: Portal-themed staff tools and alliance confirmation
synopsis: Staff workspaces follow portal appearance; alliance creation and restoration are clearer.
changes: Staff workspaces match the current portal theme and keep the gameplay theme separate.
Restore an alliance is always expanded. Successful alliance creation shows an Owner confirmation box with disclosure status.
The standalone Reset round tab is removed from Staff panel; round controls remain in Admin Controlcenter.
Staff workspace bootstrap is bundled into the established portal and game loading paths.

title: Compact portal release ledger
synopsis: The portal changelog displays the ten newest versions, while the news archive retains older releases.
changes: Portal version changelog shows only the latest ten releases.
Historical release articles remain available through the news archive.

title: Portal staff workspaces and optional original view
synopsis: Administration moves to the portal so staff can keep playing their own planet.
changes: Staff panel owns Admin Controlcenter, Alliance Controlcenter, Multihunters and support alongside users and news administration.
Dedicated staff workspaces use a separate browser save and do not automatically advance the staff gameplay planet or submit its fleet snapshots.
The ingame Administration menu is hidden by default. Staff panel provides a toggle and link to the original ingame staff view.
Existing administrator API permissions still protect every staff operation.

title: Staff structure workspace and simulated battle lab
synopsis: Visible structure slots, staff generation and test battles connect the Uplink, Journal and calculator.
changes: Alliance Controlcenter Structures shows slots 11–15, current occupants and construction progress, plus a staff generator for the selected alliance.
Staff can queue a three-tick build or immediately activate a timed structure. Occupied slots, invalid coordinates and duplicate active types are rejected.
Satelite Uplink includes a random simulated battle lab. Reports also appear in Journal and load the original fleets into the battle calculator.
Simulation changes no real fleets, resources, asteroids or Multihunter movement evidence.

title: Portal account access and requested alliance reset
synopsis: Account signup and sign-in are easier to find; the requested alliance reset clears old registrations and keys.
changes: User Profile includes Create account. Portal has a themed right-side login/registration prompt and signed-in account links.
Requested one-time alliance reset removes alliance registrations, Owner keys and disclosure phrases; accounts and planet/ruler identities are preserved.
Planet affiliations become Unaffiliated and stale alliance UI is cleared when central data refreshes.

title: Alliance creation and global keyholder audit
synopsis: Configure new alliance messages and optional Owner-authorised disclosure at creation; staff keyholders now span every alliance.
changes: Create alliance includes description, recruitment message, MOTD and an optional 12–128 character disclosure passphrase. The creator receives Owner rank and an encrypted personal key.
Alliance Controlcenter Keyholders lists all alliances, including archived registrations, independently of the selected alliance.
Each reveal uses the exact alliance and Owner pair and requires the holder-provided passphrase. Secrets remain hidden by default.

title: Multihunter fleet farming analysis
synopsis: Staff can review fleet activity between two planets with transparent evidence and data limitations.
changes: Multihunters adds Fleet farming analysis with two planet selectors and a tick range.
Authenticated launch and battle reports record mission direction, fleet size, losses and captured asteroids with duplicate protection and round separation.
The report distinguishes insufficient evidence, repeated profitable raids and mutual profitable raids; staff review is required and no automatic sanctions are applied.
Practice-browser reporting starts with this release; missing or historical events remain unknown.

title: Arcade and Classic skins, Network Hub and fleet calculator
synopsis: Nyan Cat portal art, Classic game styling and clearer fleet command tools.
changes: Nyan Cat adds generated pixel artwork, rainbow frames and an arcade starfield to portal and manual themes; it joins all-theme cycling.
Classic adds a compact old-school in-game skin with red navigation, blue panels and bevel buttons.
Fleet Add to Calc loads that fleet as attacker and opens the calculator while preserving defender inputs.
Galaxy Forum appears under Foreign Affairs. Galaxy Status is renamed Network Hub across navigation and documentation.
Network Hub separates incoming, outgoing and returning fleets with an optional permission-aware alliance intel overlay.
Alliance Controlcenter Keyholders supports Owner-authorised passphrase disclosure to staff; rotating a key invalidates its previous disclosure phrase.
Multihunters has separate Raw access log and Multi subpages with staff-only access, account IP history and 30-day retention.
User Profile labels its portal appearance submenu Portal theme settings.

title: Profile audio controls
synopsis: Portal audio controls move into User Profile theme settings.
changes: The top-of-page audio controller is hidden.
Mute and volume controls are available under User Profile → Theme settings.
Portal playback and the separate opt-in game setting remain available.

title: Desert-space ambience
synopsis: Original cinematic portal ambience with an optional in-game soundtrack.
changes: The portal has a 96-second original generated desert-space score with mute and volume controls.
In-game music defaults off and can be enabled under Planet Settings → Ambient soundtrack.
The soundtrack pauses during portal video playback and while its browser tab is hidden.
Browser autoplay restrictions are handled with a clear starts-after-click status.

title: Unified round control workspace
synopsis: One round-settings and ticker workspace with duplicate controls removed.
changes: Round settings and Ticker & state become one continuous Round & ticker workspace.
Tick interval is configured once; Run one tick appears only in ticker controls.
Planet-tool shortcuts and duplicate reset-default controls are removed from round configuration; their own subpages retain those functions.
The two extra section-navigation buttons are removed while the main Admin Controlcenter submenu remains.
Portal, game, profile, forums, staff and achievement submenus share one themed tab style.

title: Staff controlcenters and private forum achievements
synopsis: Dedicated staff subpages and private alliance and galaxy discussions.
changes: Admin Controlcenter groups Round & ticker, Planet Editor, Stats Editor, Planet tools and Havoc in a shared submenu.
Alliance Controlcenter groups Overview, Settings, Members, Ranks, Funds and Structures with an alliance selector for staff.
Staff dummy assignments and planet alliance membership move to the Alliance Controlcenter Members page.
Multihunters has matching Overview, Case queue, Reports and Tools placeholders; no investigation or ban actions are active.
Private Alliance Forums and Galaxy Forum have dedicated menu entries and author-specific forum achievements.
Staff alliance edits remain server-authorised; personal Owner passkeys are not exposed to staff.
All portal and in-game manuals include the new navigation, permissions, fleet controls and forum workflows.
Achievement automation shows persistent ON/OFF, claimed totals and last-claim confirmation; Open Bonuses now navigates correctly.

title: Alliance Launch Bay and officer readiness
synopsis: A permanent fourth fleet, private member readiness cards and configurable command permissions.
changes: Alliance Fleet is a fourth deployable slot permanently controlled from Alliance Launch Bay.
Officers can view private member idle-fleet reports by ship type in separate themed cards under Defence.
Fleet readiness and Launch Bay are independent rank permissions, enabled by default for Owner, HC and Officer.
Central launch orders are validated by membership and permissions and delivered to the member’s open practice game.
Round reset clears fleet reports and pending launch orders. Unknown and stale snapshots are labelled explicitly.
Portal and in-game manuals cover all new fleet operations, vendor sales, government effects, support tickets, theme cycling and longer scored cinematic clips.
Alliance Forums is an alliance submenu with private topics and replies linked to the alliance-forum achievement.
Galaxy Forum is private to the current galaxy and linked to its own forum achievement.

title: Fleet operations and cinematic soundtrack
synopsis: Personalised fleets, prelaunch orders, vendor sales and longer scored battle concepts.
changes: Fleet names accept distinct 3–15 character alphanumeric names.
Fleet missions support 0–12 tick delayed launch and immediate cancellation before departure. Fake Defence recalls at ETA one.
Fleet travel now considers class, travel research, same-alliance defence and fixed five-tick in-galaxy defence.
Ship Analysis displays primary-target normal damage, EMP shots and stealing damage.
Vendor sales lock Base ships for twelve ticks and keep their value until settlement; the practice buyback rate is clearly stated.
Government mining, research and construction effects now modify the practice output rates.
Three battle concepts are 24 seconds each; the montage lasts 80 seconds and all include an original generated cinematic soundtrack.
User Profile Theme settings can cycle through all six portal themes on every reload; Remember setting controls persistence.

title: Command center, support and cinematic archive
synopsis: A unified Admin Controlcenter, private support tickets and a themed multimedia archive.
changes: Current Round Setup and Round State now share Admin Controlcenter with separate configuration, ticker, snapshot and reset boxes.
User Profile has private staff-support and ban-appeal tickets with a staff queue.
Portal multimedia sits above Command Operations and contains an interface montage plus three animated AI battle concept clips.
A dedicated Rules page is linked from the footer. Non-neutral portal themes receive brighter sci-fi framing and artwork.
Waves and Satelite Uplink receive themed graphics and clearer sections; the manual documents ownership and community support.

title: Alliance ownership and community controls
synopsis: Owner ranks, secure alliance recovery, forums and refined theme controls.
changes: Alliance creators receive Owner rank; only Owners or staff can add or remove an Owner.
Alliance Settings has separate name, description, recruitment message and MOTD editors.
Personal Owner passkeys are encrypted in the central database and allow reserved-name recovery and rank-projected private intel feeds.
Account-owned alliance settings survive a reset; gameplay resources, structures, scans and intel remain reset.
Community and private alliance forums support topics and replies. Discord chat is prepared with YouSMP configuration placeholders.
Portal themes move to the User Profile Theme settings tab with Remember setting. Theme changes reload portal or game.
Buttons inherit the selected theme with clearer text; Resource uplink no longer follows page scrolling.
Navigation uses Satelite Uplink, Journal, Achievements, Current Round Setup, Planet Editor and Stats Editor throughout.

title: Alliance construction and portal theme frames
synopsis: Three-tick alliance construction and stronger illustrated portal themes.
changes: All five alliance structures take three ticks to build and reserve their placement slot while queued.
Construction costs are paid once; effects and cooldowns start after completion.
Overview has a separate themed alliance-structures module with construction and active-effect progress bars.
Portal themes use larger artwork areas, illuminated sci-fi frames and inset synopsis, profile, lore and action boxes.
Alliance permissions continue to follow the account-owned planet after identity changes.

title: Universe analysis and continuous viewscreen
synopsis: KIA-inspired universe modules and a continuous RTS command viewscreen.
changes: Universe has modular top planets, top galaxies, civilisation distribution, size gains/losses, value ratios, crashers, combat activity and tick history.
History tracks observed ticks, with a maximum 24-tick comparison window; private alliance modules require the permitted intel overlay.
The RTS-style viewscreen extends from the themed left menu through the artwork and development controls to the planet box at the right edge, for every theme.
Overview identity updates immediately from Planet Settings.
Round reset preserves planet name, ruler name and public username while retaining account-owned alliance ranks.

title: Universe feeds and command profiles
synopsis: Text gamedumps, compact race profiles and clearer commander settings.
changes: The Universe Status panel offers planet, galaxy and alliance text dumps, plus a rank-protected private intel export.
Expanded race profiles use a wider layout without an internal scrollbar.
Manual navigation expands to its full height and scrolls with the page.
Planet Settings uses separate centred identity, sharing, quest, relocation and theme boxes.
Fleet transfers support all ships or individual ship classes.
Round reset clears opt-in checkboxes while preserving public usernames.
Race names and matching theme labels are updated throughout the interface.
Staff article editing is divided into identity, typography and body boxes.
News categories have distinct hues; section separators and command headers carry more themed artwork.
Planet and ruler names have independent save controls, restricted to the account-owned planet.

title: Compact race profiles
synopsis: Five centred race cards open detailed profiles through their plus controls.
changes: Five compact race cards share a centred desktop row.
Plus controls reveal doctrine, traits, bonus references and fleet artwork.
Expanded profiles close on pointer exit, Escape or focus leaving the card; touch users can toggle the plus button.

title: Themed manual chapters
synopsis: The entire manual is reorganized into illustrated chapters with larger pictograms and shaded subsections.
changes: Large theme-specific pictograms mark every chapter, with artwork and compact reference headers.
Top-level subsections use alternating shading and custom instruction panels.
Navigation, tables, flow cards and race profiles follow the current portal theme.

title: Race encyclopedia
synopsis: The portal presents detailed race profiles, characteristics, bonus references and ship artwork.
changes: Five illustrated race cards list doctrine, stealth, recovery, CU/RP bases, production and trade reference values.
Applied startup bonuses are separated from reference modifiers that are not implemented in the practice engine.
Each race links to Shipstats and the manual bonus guide.
Race encyclopedia links to the dedicated Races & bonuses manual chapter, which links back to the portal.

title: Portal footer navigation
synopsis: A themed footer provides five future navigation slots.
changes: About, Support, Rules, Privacy and Contact are placeholders in the portal footer.
Placeholder links show a Coming soon notice without navigating to missing pages.

title: Header layout repair
synopsis: The artwork header keeps the page grid, right rail and development navigation correctly aligned.
changes: The header wrapper is restored after replacing the breadcrumb with artwork.
Header artwork and command boxes wrap within the available width instead of displacing the resource rail.
Theme nameplate text no longer splits a race name mid-word.
The Vesper Chronicles module is placed above the Version changelog, after Race command profiles.

title: Structured ship order cards
synopsis: Production cards separate combat stats, target priorities, prices and order controls.
changes: A brief combat profile lists initiative, guns, per-gun damage, armour, ETA and role.
Target priorities and a full Shipstats link appear in their own summary.
Unit costs, quantity, autofill, fleet destination and order buttons use clearer spacing and subpanels.
Portal module 02 Race command profiles sits immediately above the Version changelog.

title: Quest automation settings
synopsis: Planet Settings can automatically claim completed rewards into the bonus bank.
changes: A centered Quest automation box sits below tax and sharing controls.
Auto-claim is off by default and after reset; enabling it collects only completed, unclaimed objectives.
Resource and point allocation remains manual on the Bonuses tab.

title: Universe alliance intel filtering
synopsis: Universe alliances and filters appear only through an authorized, enabled intel overlay.
changes: Apply alliance intel controls alliance visibility and filter options.
Alliance names come only from alliance intel records, with Unknown for missing reports.
Directory alliance membership is excluded from universe search and alliance statistics when overlay is off.

title: Structured news transmissions
synopsis: News Log uses illustrated event cards with separate report and metadata boxes.
changes: Each event has a graphical icon header, readable transmission body and individual tick/date/category boxes.
Existing research, production, battle, covert and Game updates color identities remain visible.
Battle details and calculator links remain structured inside the event card.

title: Release ledger and bulk quest claims
synopsis: The changelog is a separate statistical portal module and completed quests can be claimed in groups.
changes: Release ledger displays latest version, recorded releases and change counts with a statistical visual style.
Each quest category can claim all reached, unclaimed goals at once.
A final Claim all completed quests button collects all available rewards without bypassing objectives.

title: Illustrated field manual
synopsis: The manual documents current features with artwork, operational flow cards and visual reference tables.
changes: New chapters explain draft orders, bonus allocation, ticker scheduling and staff news publishing.
Manual artwork, icon headings, step cards and category color keys improve navigation and reading.
Practice-only systems and server-backed records are clearly distinguished.

title: News category artwork
synopsis: Article categories have dedicated backgrounds and recognizable color hues.
changes: Mechanics is purple, round updates blue, stats green, errors red and pause/resume yellow.
Category backgrounds and icon accents apply to portal news cards, the archive and staff article pages.
Pinned cards retain their 24-hour emphasis within their category color scheme.

title: Illustrated development navigation
synopsis: Mining, Construction, Research, Population and Planet Settings become illustrated theme-aware cards.
changes: Development cards use the active skin artwork with activity imagery, readable title strips and illuminated icons.
All eleven skins receive matching artwork and hover/selected treatments.

title: Asteroid draft orders
synopsis: Mining supports Order now, Add to order and a combined Order all confirmation.
changes: Asteroid drafts are saved without charging resources and can be removed or cleared.
Order all validates every type and confirms the complete rising-cost bill atomically.
Independent orders remain available and existing mining limits are preserved.

title: Theme artwork and scheduled ticker
synopsis: Every skin has dedicated header artwork; automatic ticker starts use a saved date/time without quest credit.
changes: The old breadcrumb and skin badge are replaced by theme-matched header artwork.
Round state can schedule or cancel a browser-practice auto-start using local date and time.
Automatic starts create a Game updates notice but never award ticker quest progress.
The tick progress bar is more visible and shows its percentage.

title: Planet command metrics
synopsis: The planet header displays Score, XP and Value in a polished theme-aware command panel.
changes: Current Score, XP and Value update with the planet name, ruler, coordinates and tick.
The header uses a compact metric grid, illuminated theme borders and clear number alignment.

title: Quest insignia and medals
synopsis: Theme-specific goal icons, reward badges and completion medals decorate the quest board.
changes: Quest goal symbols use custom frames for every interface skin.
Resource, research, construction and asteroid rewards display matching icon badges.
Completed objectives display a medal; claimed rewards upgrade it to gold.

title: Ticker confirmations
synopsis: Ticker start, pause and stop are highlighted in Recent signals and Game updates news.
changes: Round state has a separate Stop control alongside Start, Pause and Run one tick.
Every ticker state change confirms with a toast and prominent yellow/black news event.
Game updates is a dedicated on/off news filter category.
First start, stop and restart each unlock a unique lore quest awarding one asteroid of each type, claimable once through Bonuses.
Initial rendering waits until all feature definitions are loaded.

title: Command time display
synopsis: A clear header time box shows the current tick, next tick countdown and 24-hour UTC clock.
changes: Tick values and countdown use a readable theme-aware header box.
A live UTC HH:mm:ss clock updates every second and uses military time.
Tick interval progress freezes on pause and restarts with the ticker.
The header compares local and synchronized server UTC clocks and shows page load and server round-trip milliseconds.

title: Live universe banner
synopsis: The portal banner shows central planet, asteroid and alliance totals.
changes: An integrated theme-aware status box displays current shared universe counts.
Public aggregate statistics refresh every 30 seconds without exposing private planet data.

title: Reset sharing preferences
synopsis: Quick actions uses one preference box with sharing and alliance tax off after reset.
changes: Alliance tax, alliance scan sharing and public sharing reset to unchecked.
The three Quick actions controls share one box.
Personal scans remain available when alliance sharing is disabled.
Staff-written articles now join the portal News posts cards, sorted with version news by publication date.
Staff articles remain visibly pinned for 24 hours, then return to date order automatically.

title: Staff tabs and article editing
synopsis: Staff tools are organized into tabs with a published article list and edit/save controls.
changes: Staff tabs group round controls, users, news articles and round reset.
Staff-made articles appear below the editor; Edit loads an article and Save changes updates its existing entry.
Portal assets use versioned URLs to avoid stale publishing controls.
Article storage initializes safely when its migration has not run yet.
Covert results have their own blue news category and icon.
Quick actions merges tax and both scan-sharing controls into one box; all start unchecked after round reset.

title: Covert command
synopsis: Military gains a covert operations console with agents, guards, stealth, missions and instant reports.
changes: Nine operations unlock through the existing covert research branch and apply to practice target snapshots.
Mission costs, stealth, success checks, target alert and operation effects use Planetarion manual rules.
Personnel training and wages use explicitly labelled Starfall practice rates.
Quest bonus tab imports a one-time race-adjusted Planetarion startup grant and shows current balances.

title: Quest reward bank
synopsis: Review quest lore and rewards, then allocate unused resources, asteroids, research and construction bonuses.
changes: Every supported quest displays its lore and reward before completion.
Claimed rewards enter a persistent bonus bank under Quests; resource and asteroid rewards are accepted explicitly.
Research and construction allocations support partial progress and multiple completions with budget and cap validation.
Staff article editor fills the module width, with bold, italic, font and size controls and a right-aligned publish button.
News Log distinguishes green research, orange production and light-red battle reports.
Battle reports have a dedicated on/off news category filter.
Quest board and Bonuses are separate tabs in the same tab bar style as Alliance.
Planetarion startup bonuses are imported once, adjusted by race, and displayed as current unused balances; no unverified loyalty bonus is added.

title: Staff news publishing
synopsis: Create categorized articles from the staff panel with dedicated icons and public archive links.
changes: Game admins can publish titles, synopses and article text to the central database.
Five update categories each have a theme icon on the editor, news cards and article pages.
Public portal and news archive display staff articles newest first; article text is rendered safely.

title: Draft orders and fleet delivery
synopsis: Build a multi-ship draft, confirm it with Order all, and choose where each ship is delivered.
changes: Ship cards separate Order now from Add to order.
Add to order saves a draft without charging resources; Order all validates and confirms the complete draft atomically.
Each ship has a Base / Fleet 1–3 delivery choice, applied when production finishes.
Drafts can be reviewed, removed or cleared and survive reloads.
Adaptive sidebar spacing, structured combat news and calculator import.
Round state ticker start, pause, step and speed controls for the browser practice round.
Alliance news has a distinct icon and theme accent in both signal lists; Quick actions preferences have quests.

title: Population and government ship production
synopsis: Running ship orders now apply population and government production bonuses with a manual lookup.
changes: Shipwright allocation and government output bonuses add together and immediately update active order rates and ETA.
Population includes a government selector and a linked manual lookup.
Democracy and Totalitarianism cost discounts apply to new ship orders without repricing paid orders.
Government changes use a 72-tick revolution production penalty.

title: Planet command header
synopsis: Your planet identity and current tick are grouped in a theme-matched top-right command box.
changes: Top-right box shows home coordinates, planet name, ruler and current tick.
The box updates after planet edits, relocation and tick progression, and adapts to narrow screens.
Whole-round reset also clears claimed quest rewards and restores quest progress to the default round.
Quest checkmarks follow claimed rewards and all clear when the round is reset.

title: Round state reset control
synopsis: Round state has a separate Reset round panel with an explicit confirmation.
changes: Round state includes a dedicated game-admin Reset round box.
Reset opens Are you sure? and requires typing RESET before the entire round is regenerated.
Apply changes buttons in the planet modules have improved theme contrast.

title: Complete round reset defaults
synopsis: A reset restores the default race, fleet catalogue and support panels correctly.
changes: Fresh rounds explicitly initialize race, galaxy fund, quest claims and news filters.
The shared directory normalizes fleet identifiers after a reset so the base fleet editor displays the correct ships.

title: Independent planet editor modules
synopsis: Each planet editor module applies its own changes without modifying other fields.
changes: Separate identity, location, alliance, resources, asteroids, base fleet, experience, structures and status modules.
Every module has an Apply changes button and its own confirmation status.
Applying one module preserves unsaved values in the other modules.

title: Portal account and round controls
synopsis: Registration, user profiles and staff controls join the portal navigation.
changes: Top navigation includes Shipstats and News, plus Register / Sign up for guests and User profile for signed-in commanders.
Admin-only staff controls list accounts and assign available planets.
Users can save their public name and portal theme through User profile.
Admin round reset clears and regenerates shared planets, alliances, intel, scans and browser news while preserving accounts and passwords.
Reset generations prevent stale clients from re-uploading scans from a previous round.

title: Admin alliance membership repair
synopsis: Admin-assigned planets now appear in the correct alliance roster, including after reload.
changes: Member rosters are reconciled with centrally assigned planets for every alliance.
Stable planet IDs retain roles across planet renames and remove memberships from the old alliance when moved.
Existing missing member records are repaired when loading the shared directory.

title: Version list and code references
synopsis: The v0.53.0 article now presents release changes as a dated version list with readable code references.
changes: The v0.53.0 news article uses a chronological version list, newest first.
Each version includes its change list and short code snippets with reference links.

title: Intel nicknames
synopsis: Alliance intel now supports nicknames and suggestions for members awaiting planet assignment.
changes: Nickname column provides a free-text box with suggestions for unassigned alliance members.
Nicknames are stored centrally for your alliance and follow intel edit and visible-field permissions.
Nickname labels do not change actual alliance membership or planet assignments.
Users can set their public game username beneath Planet display name; login credentials are unchanged.
Galaxy Browser Intel overlay mirrors alliance intel nickname, alliance, relation and scan columns in display-only mode.
Apply to order # assigns the chosen factories to the active ship order without resetting progress or changing queued orders.
codeSnippets:
// Apply factories to the active ship order
applyFactoriesToOrder(state.production.orderNumber);

title: Command news archive
synopsis: News cards now match Command Operations, with short briefings and a dated archive linking to full articles.
changes: Portal news posts use the same themed card layout as Command Operations.
Each news card includes a short synopsis and a link to its complete article.
The news archive lists releases by date, newest first, with version numbers.
Alliance Intel relations are read-only text, with War in bold red. The redundant Open Intel column is removed; planet names and scan letters open dossiers.
News cards include sci-fi background illustrations with dark overlays for readable text.
codeSnippets:
// Dated news articles are generated from release entries
newsPath(release); // /news-v0-52-0.html

title: Alliance intel and fleet launch
changes: Alliance dropdowns list all in-game alliances without changing actual membership.
Relation selectors color intel rows: Ally green, War red, NAP orange.
Latest available scans appear as linked type letters, respecting rank visibility.
Portal News posts and a versioned changelog added below Command Operations.
Fixed Fleet 1–3 launch selections; missions now move ships into outbound orders with ETA and return correctly.
Galaxy Scan uses radio buttons and All scans, charging once for the complete sweep of unlocked scan types.
synopsis: Alliance intel gains diplomatic colors and scan links; Fleet Launch is fixed and Galaxy Scan offers All scans.

title: Shared command network
changes: Central planet directory shared by the ordinary and alliance intel browsers.
Central alliance intel with rank permissions, visible field controls and galaxy overlay.
Version notification beneath the left game menu.
Alliance fund donation and exchange with 5% loss and minimum reserve controls.
Alliance statistics replace creation after founding; futuristic portal and manual styles.
synopsis: A shared planet directory, protected alliance intel and configurable rank visibility connect the command network.
codeSnippets:
// Load the shared planet directory
await centralDirectoryRequest("/api/planets");

title: Fleet reference
changes: Dedicated Shipstats manual page with race table colors, ship artwork and resource icons.
synopsis: The fleet reference adds a dedicated Shipstats page with race colors, ship artwork and resource icons.
